metadata.repo_type_justification: Application source with an HTTP request entry point (Timesheet.aspx.vb, System.Web.UI.Page) plus runtime configuration (web.config); no IaC or CI/CD present.
metadata.archetype_justification: Direct SQL Server connection performing both SELECT reads and INSERT writes on the timesheets entity keyed by session employee_id.

tech_stack.architecture: Single-server IIS 6 monolith with code-behind SQL data access

findings.title: Documented API Interface
findings.description: Only integration surface is the ASP.NET WebForms page Timesheet.aspx.vb, whose Page_Load and btnSave_Click postback handlers read and write SQL directly. No REST controller, GraphQL schema, AsyncAPI spec, or Smithy model exists in the repository.
findings.gap: Integration requires UI automation of ViewState postbacks or direct SQL Server access - brittle and non-auditable.
findings.recommendation: Extract the read and insert logic into a service layer and expose it as a versioned HTTP API.

blocker_remediation.immediate: Extract the read and insert logic into a service layer and expose it as a versioned HTTP API.
blocker_remediation.target_state: Control present and verifiable at the agent-facing integration surface.

findings.title: Idempotent Write Operations
findings.description: btnSave_Click issues an unconditional INSERT INTO timesheets with no idempotency key, no business-key uniqueness check, and no read-before-write.
findings.gap: No idempotency mechanism in the write path; a retried submit creates duplicate timesheet rows.
findings.recommendation: Add a unique constraint on (employee_id, entry_date, project) and accept a caller-supplied idempotency key.

ara_metadata.conditional_resolution: Resolved to BLOCKER: agent_scope=write-enabled and the write path has no idempotency mechanism.
ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: A retried agent tool call against btnSave_Click duplicates timesheet rows, so the gap is gated as a blocker under write-enabled scope.

blocker_remediation.immediate: Add a unique constraint on (employee_id, entry_date, project) and accept a caller-supplied idempotency key.
blocker_remediation.target_state: Control present and verifiable at the agent-facing integration surface.

findings.title: Machine Identity Authentication
findings.description: web.config configures only interactive Forms authentication (loginUrl=Login.aspx, requireSSL=false); the identity used by the data layer is Session("EmployeeId"). No OAuth2 client-credentials flow, API key with principal attribution, or mTLS exists.
findings.gap: No machine principal can authenticate and no non-human caller can be attributed.
findings.recommendation: Introduce an identity provider issuing service-principal tokens and accept bearer tokens at the API boundary.

blocker_remediation.immediate: Introduce an identity provider issuing service-principal tokens and accept bearer tokens at the API boundary.
blocker_remediation.target_state: Control present and verifiable at the agent-facing integration surface.

findings.title: Immutable Audit Logging
findings.description: The INSERT in btnSave_Click executes with no log record of the acting principal. web.config declares no trace, health-monitoring, or log sink, and customErrors mode=Off routes failures to the browser.
findings.gap: No audit trail at all, let alone an immutable, tamper-evident one.
findings.recommendation: Write append-only audit records (principal, operation, entity key) to immutable storage with retention policy.

ara_metadata.conditional_resolution: Resolved to BLOCKER: agent_scope=write-enabled and no audit record is produced for writes.
ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: Write-enabled agents require principal attribution for every mutation; none exists, so the gap is gated as a blocker.

blocker_remediation.immediate: Write append-only audit records (principal, operation, entity key) to immutable storage with retention policy.
blocker_remediation.target_state: Control present and verifiable at the agent-facing integration surface.

findings.title: Compensation and Rollback
findings.description: btnSave_Click executes a single ExecuteNonQuery then rebinds the grid. There is no SqlTransaction, no TransactionScope, no undo endpoint, and no compensating transaction.
findings.gap: Failures after the insert leave the write committed with no rollback path; multi-step agent workflows cannot be unwound.
findings.recommendation: Wrap writes in an explicit transaction scope and expose a reversal (void/correct) operation.

ara_metadata.conditional_resolution: Resolved to BLOCKER: agent_scope=write-enabled and no transaction or compensation exists.
ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: Agent-initiated writes cannot be undone, so the gap is gated as a blocker under write-enabled scope.

blocker_remediation.immediate: Wrap writes in an explicit transaction scope and expose a reversal (void/correct) operation.
blocker_remediation.target_state: Control present and verifiable at the agent-facing integration surface.

findings.title: Sensitive Data Classification
findings.description: Employee-attributable timesheet records are persisted in SQL Server. BindGrid() binds the raw DataTable from a SELECT directly to gridEntries with no DTO, field exclusion, or projection control, so consumers receive whatever columns the query returns. Authorization is a single role-less Forms-auth session, and no classification tags or field annotations exist.
findings.gap: No response-scoping layer between the database and the consumer, and no sensitive vs non-sensitive access differentiation.
findings.recommendation: Replace raw DataTable binding with explicit DTOs enumerating allowed fields, and add scoped permissions for employee-identifying fields.

ara_metadata.conditional_resolution: Resolved to BLOCKER: agent_scope=write-enabled and B1 fired - raw DataTable binding returns unscoped employee data.
ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: B1 fired because BindGrid() binds the unprojected SELECT result directly to the grid; under write-enabled scope B1 resolves to BLOCKER.

b1.reasoning: Raw DataTable from SELECT bound directly to gridEntries - no DTO, field exclusion, or projection control.

b2.reasoning: Single role-less Forms-auth session; no scope or role differentiates sensitive from non-sensitive access.

b3.reasoning: No classification tags, field annotations, or PII detection tooling present.

blocker_remediation.immediate: Replace raw DataTable binding with explicit DTOs enumerating allowed fields, and add scoped permissions for employee-identifying fields.
blocker_remediation.target_state: Control present and verifiable at the agent-facing integration surface.

findings.title: Data Residency and Sovereignty
findings.description: Employee timesheet data (worker-attributable labour records) is stored on a single fixed-IP SQL Server (Data Source=10.0.6.15). No residency policy, region configuration, replication boundary, or GDPR/LGPD reference appears in web.config or README.md.
findings.gap: No declared or enforced residency boundary, so there is no basis for deciding whether this data may be sent to an out-of-region model endpoint.
findings.recommendation: Document the jurisdiction and residency classification of the Timesheets database and enforce egress constraints.

ara_metadata.conditional_resolution: Resolved to BLOCKER: agent_scope=write-enabled and the persisted employee data has no declared residency boundary.
ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: Worker labour records are personal data with no stated jurisdiction, so transmission decisions are ungoverned; gated as a blocker under write-enabled scope.

blocker_remediation.immediate: Document the jurisdiction and residency classification of the Timesheets database and enforce egress constraints.
blocker_remediation.target_state: Control present and verifiable at the agent-facing integration surface.

findings.title: Scoped Permissions (Least Privilege)
findings.description: All callers authenticate through one Forms-auth flow, and the application connects to SQL Server as the single shared login ts_app. There are no roles, no <authorization> section, and no per-principal policy.
findings.gap: No mechanism exists to grant a read-only, resource-scoped identity.
findings.recommendation: Introduce role-based authorization and distinct database principals per access level.

findings.title: Action-Level Authorization
findings.description: Neither BindGrid() (read) nor btnSave_Click (write) performs a permission check; both execute for any authenticated session. No canRead/canWrite checks or method-level authorization exist.
findings.gap: Read access cannot be granted without implicitly granting write access.
findings.recommendation: Add explicit per-operation authorization checks before each data access call.

findings.title: Identity Propagation and Delegation
findings.description: Identity is carried as Session("EmployeeId") in an InProc session. No token is parsed, no Authorization header is handled, and there is no way to distinguish an acting principal from a data subject.
findings.gap: On-behalf-of flows are impossible; a caller would have to assume a human's session.
findings.recommendation: Adopt token-based identity with separate actor and subject claims.

findings.title: Credential Management
findings.description: The SQL Server password is hardcoded in plaintext in web.config (User ID=ts_app;Password=Time2006!). The configuration section is not encrypted, no secrets manager or Vault integration exists, and there is no rotation mechanism. debug=true and customErrors mode=Off widen exposure on error pages.
findings.gap: A static, shared, plaintext production credential committed to source control with no rotation.
findings.recommendation: Rotate the exposed password immediately and move the credential to a managed secrets store with scheduled rotation.

findings.title: Agent Identity Suspension
findings.description: No API key store, role deactivation path, or per-principal disable mechanism exists. Revoking access means rotating the shared ts_app credential or taking the single IIS site offline.
findings.gap: One misbehaving caller cannot be isolated without affecting all users.
findings.recommendation: Issue per-principal credentials with an immediate revocation path.

findings.title: Concurrency Controls
findings.description: The INSERT uses no version column, no If-Match/ETag, no SELECT ... FOR UPDATE, and no conditional write. Session/ViewState is the only coordination mechanism.
findings.gap: Concurrent callers can create conflicting or duplicate entries for the same employee and date.
findings.recommendation: Add optimistic concurrency (row version) plus a unique business-key constraint.

ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: The repository exposes write operations (INSERT in btnSave_Click), so agent_scope was inferred as write-enabled and this question evaluates at its RISK severity.

findings.title: Circuit Breakers and Resilience
findings.description: SqlConnection and SqlCommand are used with default timeouts and no retry, backoff, or circuit breaker. No resilience library is declared (the repository contains no dependency manifest).
findings.gap: SQL Server slowness propagates directly to callers as hung requests.
findings.recommendation: Add explicit command timeouts and a retry/circuit-breaker policy around data access.

findings.title: Rate Limiting and Throttling
findings.description: web.config declares no request-rate or handler limits, and no API gateway or WAF is defined anywhere in the repository. The app runs on a single IIS 6 host with InProc session state.
findings.gap: A looping caller can saturate the single server and its SQL Server instance.
findings.recommendation: Enforce per-principal request rate limits at an edge proxy or gateway.

findings.title: Blast Radius and Transaction Limits
findings.description: No business-domain caps exist - no maximum entries per session, no hours ceiling, no bulk-size limit. txtHours.Text is interpolated into the SQL numeric position with no bound check.
findings.gap: No limit on the number or magnitude of writes a single caller can produce.
findings.recommendation: Add configurable per-principal write quotas and database range constraints on hours.

ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: The repository exposes write operations (INSERT in btnSave_Click), so agent_scope was inferred as write-enabled and this question evaluates at its RISK severity.

findings.title: PII Redaction in Logs
findings.description: customErrors mode=Off combined with debug=true renders a full ASP.NET error page on failure, including the concatenated SQL text that embeds Session("EmployeeId"), txtDate.Text, and txtProject.Text. No masking or scrubbing exists.
findings.gap: Employee-attributable values are exposed in error output with no redaction.
findings.recommendation: Set customErrors mode=On and debug=false, then add structured logging with field-level PII masking.

findings.title: Draft/Pending State
findings.description: The insert writes only employee_id, entry_date, hours, and project - there is no status column and no create-then-confirm sequence. Every write commits immediately.
findings.gap: No reviewable intermediate state for a proposed entry.
findings.recommendation: Add a status field with a DRAFT/SUBMITTED lifecycle.

ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: The repository exposes write operations (INSERT in btnSave_Click), so agent_scope was inferred as write-enabled and this question evaluates at its RISK severity.

findings.title: Configurable Approval Gates
findings.description: No approval endpoint, confirmation step, or operation-level flag exists; btnSave_Click is the terminal action.
findings.gap: No per-operation human approval can be configured.
findings.recommendation: Introduce an approval workflow for agent-originated writes.

ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: The repository exposes write operations (INSERT in btnSave_Click), so agent_scope was inferred as write-enabled and this question evaluates at its RISK severity.

findings.title: Machine-Readable API Specification
findings.description: No OpenAPI, Swagger, GraphQL, AsyncAPI, or Smithy artifact exists. Searched all repository files by name pattern and inspected the only source file; the surface is an .aspx postback page.
findings.gap: No machine-readable contract from which agent tool definitions can be generated.
findings.recommendation: Generate an OpenAPI document once an HTTP API exists (API-Q1).

findings.title: Structured Error Responses
findings.description: No Try/Catch surrounds the SQL calls, and customErrors mode=Off returns an HTML stack-trace page rather than a machine-readable error body with a code and retryability indicator.
findings.gap: Callers cannot distinguish retriable from terminal failures.
findings.recommendation: Return a JSON error envelope with code, message, and a retryable flag.

findings.title: Queryable Current State
findings.description: Current state is readable only as rendered HTML: BindGrid() selects entry_date, hours, project for the session employee and binds it to a grid. No programmatic read endpoint exists.
findings.gap: State inspection requires scraping a ViewState-heavy HTML page.
findings.recommendation: Promote the BindGrid() query to a documented read-only API.

findings.title: Selective Query Support
findings.description: BindGrid() issues an unbounded SELECT ... ORDER BY entry_date DESC with no TOP, no paging, and no filter parameters.
findings.gap: No pagination, filtering, or result-size cap.
findings.recommendation: Add limit/offset and date-range filters to the read path.

findings.title: Input Validation and Schema Enforcement
findings.description: No validation exists. txtDate.Text, txtHours.Text, txtProject.Text, and Session("EmployeeId") are concatenated directly into SQL strings on both the read and write paths; hours is interpolated unquoted and is neither type- nor range-checked. Both statements are SQL-injectable, as the file's own comment acknowledges.
findings.gap: No schema enforcement or field-level rejection, plus SQL injection exposure on read and write.
findings.recommendation: Replace string-concatenated SQL with parameterized SqlParameter commands and add typed range validation returning field-level errors.

findings.title: Temporal Metadata and Freshness
findings.description: The columns written are employee_id, entry_date, hours, project - entry_date is user-supplied business data. There is no created_at/updated_at, no UTC normalization, and no cache or freshness header.
findings.gap: No record-provenance timestamps and no freshness signalling.
findings.recommendation: Add UTC audit timestamps to the entity and expose them in responses.

findings.title: Schema Versioning and API Contracts
findings.description: No migration files, schema registry, JSON Schema, or versioned path exists; the timesheets table shape is implied only by inline SQL. No changelog or deprecation notice, and with no CI there is no breaking-change detection.
findings.gap: Schema and contract are undocumented and unversioned; changes are silent.
findings.recommendation: Introduce migration-managed schema and a versioned API contract.

findings.title: Distributed Tracing and Structured Logging
findings.description: No tracing or logging instrumentation: the source imports only System, System.Data, System.Data.SqlClient, and System.Configuration, and web.config declares no trace, healthMonitoring, or log provider. No correlation ID is generated or propagated.
findings.gap: Requests cannot be correlated or reconstructed after failure.
findings.recommendation: Add structured logging with a per-request correlation ID, then trace-context propagation.

findings.title: Alerting on Error Rates and Latency
findings.description: No alarm, monitor, or alerting integration exists in the repository - there is no IaC, no monitoring configuration in web.config, and no monitoring dependency.
findings.gap: Degradation is detected only by user report.
findings.recommendation: Define error-rate and latency thresholds with alert routing.

findings.title: Infrastructure Governance for Agent-Facing Surface
findings.description: No IaC of any kind exists (no Terraform, CloudFormation, CDK, Helm, or Ansible files). README.md states deployment is a manual Visual Studio 2005 publish to a network share onto a single IIS 6 / Windows Server 2003 host. No drift detection and no reviewed change path.
findings.gap: The integration surface is configured manually and is unreproducible.
findings.recommendation: Define the hosting, network, and identity surface as code under peer review.

findings.title: CI/CD with API Contract Testing
findings.description: No pipeline definitions exist (no .github/workflows, .gitlab-ci.yml, Jenkinsfile, or buildspec.yml); README.md confirms there is no build pipeline. Contract testing is therefore impossible.
findings.gap: Breaking changes reach production undetected.
findings.recommendation: Establish a build pipeline, then add API contract tests.

findings.title: Rollback Capability
findings.description: Deployment is a manual file-copy publish to a network share. There is no blue/green configuration, versioned artifact, feature flag, or traffic-shifting layer.
findings.gap: Rollback requires re-publishing from a developer workstation, with unbounded recovery time.
findings.recommendation: Produce versioned deployment artifacts with an automated rollback step.

findings.title: API Test Coverage
findings.description: No test files, test project, or test framework reference exists in the repository; the only code file is the page code-behind.
findings.gap: No automated verification of input handling, output shape, or error behaviour.
findings.recommendation: Add tests against the extracted service layer covering validation and error cases.

findings.title: Encryption at Rest for Agent-Accessible Data
findings.description: The connection string specifies no encryption options and the store is SQL Server 2005 on Windows Server 2003. No KMS or key-management configuration exists. requireSSL=false additionally leaves the forms-auth cookie unencrypted in transit.
findings.gap: No encryption at rest for employee timesheet data.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to a supported database engine with managed encryption keys.

findings.title: Sandbox/Staging Environment
findings.description: Only one configuration exists, pointing at the single production host 10.0.6.15. There is no staging or sandbox config, no docker-compose, and no seed or synthetic data script.
findings.gap: No non-production environment in which to test agent behaviour.
findings.recommendation: Create environment-specific configuration and a seeded staging database.

findings.title: Structured Response Format
findings.description: Responses are server-rendered HTML - gridEntries.DataBind() emits a WebForms grid with ViewState, which README.md notes makes pages multi-megabyte. No JSON or content-negotiated serialization exists.
findings.gap: No machine-friendly response format.
findings.recommendation: Emit JSON from the extracted service layer.

findings.title: Event Emission for State Changes
findings.description: The insert emits no event - there is no webhook, SNS/SQS/Kafka publish, or CDC mechanism.
findings.gap: No event emission for state changes; agents must poll.
findings.recommendation: Publish a domain event on timesheet creation if event-reactive agents are planned.

findings.title: Rate Limit Documentation and Headers
findings.description: No rate limits are documented and no rate-limit or Retry-After headers are returned; there is no gateway, WAF, or limiting configuration.
findings.gap: Callers have no self-throttling signal.
findings.recommendation: Publish limits and return Retry-After once throttling is introduced (STATE-Q5).

findings.title: Data Quality Awareness
findings.description: No data-quality metric, profiling report, null-rate monitor, or duplicate detection exists, and there is no uniqueness constraint on the timesheet business key.
findings.gap: Dataset trustworthiness is unmeasured.
findings.recommendation: Baseline duplicate and completeness rates before agent use.

findings.title: Semantically Meaningful Field Names
findings.description: Field names are self-describing: employee_id, entry_date, hours, project. No cryptic legacy codes appear in the SQL.
findings.gap: None material - naming is already interpretable without a data dictionary.
findings.recommendation: Preserve these names when exposing an API.

findings.title: Data Catalog / Metadata Layer
findings.description: No data catalog or metadata layer exists; the only description of the data is README.md prose and the inline SQL column list.
findings.gap: Semantics must be inferred from source code.
findings.recommendation: Document the timesheet entity in a catalog or data dictionary.

evaluations.title: Asynchronous Operation Support
evaluations.reason: Extended question not triggered - both operations are single short-lived SQL statements in Timesheet.aspx.vb; no operation exceeds 30s and no long-running workflow exists.

evaluations.title: Graceful Degradation Signaling
evaluations.reason: Extended question not triggered - no priority was supplied in context and the repository provides no evidence of P0 or critical-path designation.

evaluations.title: Business Outcome Metrics
evaluations.reason: No metrics or telemetry of any kind are emitted (no metric publication, dashboard, or instrumentation surface) - informational signal with no evidence on either side, so no finding emitted.

items.summary: Establish an API surface with machine identity, auditability, idempotent and transactional writes, and scoped/governed data access before any agent integration.
Close integration-quality gaps that make agent behaviour unpredictable: input validation and parameterized SQL, structured errors, pagination, schema versioning, tracing, and alerting.
Modernize engineering and platform maturity - IaC, CI/CD, rollback, encryption at rest, tests - plus the informational response-format and catalog improvements.

recommended_actions.action: Extract a versioned HTTP API from the WebForms code-behind
recommended_actions.rationale: Every other agent-facing control depends on a callable, documented interface; today the only surface is a ViewState postback page.

recommended_actions.action: Introduce machine identity with scoped permissions and immutable audit logging
recommended_actions.rationale: Forms auth plus a single shared SQL login gives no attributable, revocable, scopeable principal for a non-human caller.

recommended_actions.action: Parameterize all SQL and add input validation
recommended_actions.rationale: Both the read and write statements are built by string concatenation and are injectable, with no type or range checks on hours.

recommended_actions.action: Rotate the committed database credential and move it to a secrets store
recommended_actions.rationale: The production SQL password is in plaintext in web.config under source control with no rotation.

recommended_actions.action: Make writes safe: transactions, idempotency keys, and concurrency control
recommended_actions.rationale: Writes are single non-transactional inserts with no idempotency, no versioning, and no reviewable intermediate state.

recommended_actions.action: Establish IaC, CI/CD, rollback, and encryption at rest
recommended_actions.rationale: Manual VS 2005 publish onto unsupported IIS 6 / SQL Server 2005 leaves no reproducible, recoverable, or encrypted platform.

recommended_actions.action: Instrument observability: correlation IDs, structured logs, alerting, PII masking
recommended_actions.rationale: There is no logging at all, while customErrors=Off leaks employee data in error pages.
